findings.claim: Entries inside ``` and ~~~ fences are skipped (src/kmctl/checks.py:72-78); test_check_ignores_entries_in_code_fences fails without it.
Targets that resolve outside the index's folder are dropped (src/kmctl/checks.py:84); test_check_ignores_links_that_leave_the_folder covers it.
_visible filters hidden parts for docs/ pages and section concepts, prototypes skip dot-folders; test_check_skips_hidden_pages covers docs/ and a section.
Indexes are read as UTF-8 and a decode error becomes an "index is not UTF-8 text" finding with exit 1; test_check_reports_non_utf8_index covers it.
Finding has an Attributes section and a Literal level; _rel, _section_concepts and the test helpers have docstrings and return types.
tests/test_help.py checks every verb's help at 80 columns, a first line ending in a full stop, a metavar per option and an Examples epilog.

The fence tracking toggles on any line starting with ``` or ~~~, so it ignores the CommonMark rule that a fence closes only on the same character, at least as long as the opener. A ````md fence that shows a ``` example (the usual way to show markdown that contains a fence) flips the state, and the example entry after it is reported as "entry links example.md, which does not exist" (probed - docs/README.md:7). The same happens for ``` inside ~~~. Fix - remember the opener's character and length and close only on a matching line. Non-blocking because the fix is a few mechanical lines plus one test, and the common single-fence case already works.

When .okf/index.md is not UTF-8, check_okf sets linked to an empty set, so every section is also reported as "section is not linked from .okf/index.md". Those findings are noise behind the one real cause. Skip the unlinked-section findings when the root index cannot be read. Non-blocking - the real cause is still reported and the exit code is right.
The new helper _read has no docstring, against the same rule f5 applied to the other helpers. Non-blocking - a one-line docstring.

verdict.text: All six round-1 findings are fixed, each with a test that fails without the fix, and the gates are green.
The fence fix is incomplete for nested fences (f7), which still gives a false failure on an index that shows a fenced markdown example.
That and two small items are plain fixes, so the label is fix.
Read src/kmctl/checks.py, tests/test_check.py, tests/test_help.py and the check verb in src/kmctl/__init__.py in full.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format and tests pass, eval rows r1 to r6 pass, "stamp green: 4d13ec08deff784f6c8690323c9ce91a815180e69cd24aca5e96f35f0dbb469b".
Rows r1 to r6: the tests are unchanged from round 1 and still assert each row's fails_when.
The fixes did not weaken them.
Checked that each new test fails without its fix: the fence and out-of-folder tests link files that do not exist, and the hidden-pages test adds files the old rglob would report.

Probed in a scratch repo: a ```` fence holding a ``` example (false failure, f7), a non-UTF-8 root index (extra unlinked-section findings, f8), and a non-UTF-8 section index (one finding, exit 1). Ran `kmctl check` on this repo: pass.

f2 resolved: out-of-folder links are no longer entries.
f3 resolved: one hidden rule now applies to docs/, sections and prototypes.
